- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (drop >0.5 in sentiment change), model overreacts; reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or bearish (≤0.33) and news volume is low, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (±0.33 change over 3–5 days); apply +1–2% correction to forecast.
- If sentiment is bullish but news volume is low, model overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts by 1–3 days; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
